column3: Close to the Greek; “arise into the midst” is rendered “Step forward.”
NKJV includes “as whole as the other,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text ends with “his hand was restored.”
Close to the Greek; “diseases” is rendered “afflictions.”
NKJV lacks “whom He also named apostles,” as does the Textus Receptus; the critical text includes it.
NKJV includes “to heal sicknesses,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has only “to cast out demons.” “Authority” is rendered “power.”
NKJV lacks “And He appointed the Twelve,” as does the Textus Receptus; the critical text includes it.
NKJV adds “And they went into a house” at the end of this verse; the critical text places these words at the start of verse 20.
NKJV begins this verse with “Then the multitude came together”; the words about entering a house are in verse 19.
Close to the Greek; “crazy” is rendered “out of His mind.”
NKJV spells the name “Beelzebub”; the critical text has “Beelzebul.”
NKJV has “eternal condemnation,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “eternal sin.”
